analyst.summary: Solar Industries India has genuinely transformed from an industrial-explosives maker into a fast-growing defence-ammunition and rocket-systems supplier -- FY26 revenue grew 30% and profit grew 35%, with defence revenue nearly doubling and now a quarter of the business. The order book of Rs 21,300 crore is real and growing, but only covers about 18 months of the company's own FY27 revenue target, meaning future growth depends on winning fresh large contracts that are not yet signed. The stock trades at roughly 90-100 times trailing earnings, more than double what fully-valued defence public-sector peers command, and the business has also seen two fatal explosions at its explosives plants in the last three years. We rate this a Sell on valuation and risk grounds, not because the underlying business is weak -- it is a strong business priced for a level of flawless, uninterrupted execution that even a very good company will struggle to sustain indefinitely.
